themes.label: GARCH(p,q) definition and ARCH generalization
themes.need: What is the GARCH(p,q) process, why was it introduced as a generalization of ARCH, and how is it formally specified (regression form, ARCH(infinity) representation, ARMA-type representation, special cases)?
themes.distributed_justification: The motivating background/contribution (intro, split around a footnote) and the formal model specification (section 2) jointly answer one practitioner question about what GARCH is and why it exists; the roadmap sentence (b004, 24-25) between them is purely navigational and is excluded.

themes.label: GARCH(p,q) stationarity condition and proof
themes.need: Under what condition is a GARCH(p,q) process wide-sense stationary (Theorem 1), and how is this condition derived?
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 1 is stated in section 2 but its full proof is deferred to Appendix A.1 (split into three spans by conversion-residue trash at 402-403 and 454-455); together they answer one need: verifying and understanding the stationarity condition.

themes.label: GARCH(1,1) moment existence and kurtosis
themes.need: For a GARCH(1,1) process (and low-order variants), what is the condition for existence of higher-order (2m-th) moments, what do the resulting moment and kurtosis formulas look like, and how is this derived?
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 2 and its consequences (section 3) are extended by a footnote generalizing the fourth-moment condition to GARCH(1,2)/(2,1) (section 4, b020) and proved in Appendix A.2 (b045); all serve the single need of determining and understanding when higher moments exist.

themes.label: Mean and median lag in GARCH(1,1)
themes.need: How is the mean/median lag of the GARCH(1,1) conditional variance equation computed, and how does it compare across competing lag specifications in an applied fit?
themes.distributed_justification: The lag formulas are derived in section 3 (mean lag, then median lag sharing a paragraph with a fourth-moment-condition clause) and then applied/compared for the fitted models in section 7's empirical example -- one coherent need about interpreting model memory length.

themes.label: ML estimation of the GARCH regression model
themes.need: How is the GARCH regression model estimated by maximum likelihood -- what are the score and information-matrix expressions, the iterative BHHH algorithm, and its asymptotic properties under weaker distributional assumptions?

themes.label: ACF/PACF diagnostics for GARCH
themes.need: How do the autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions of the squared process help identify and diagnose GARCH behavior in the conditional variance equation?
themes.distributed_justification: The fourth-moment-condition footnote (b020, 181-194) interrupts the ACF/PACF discussion physically but belongs to the moment-existence need (t03); the ACF/PACF motivation and derivation resume immediately after it.

themes.label: Lagrange multiplier test for GARCH
themes.need: How do you formally test for the presence of GARCH effects using the Lagrange multiplier test, and why is a fully general test infeasible?

themes.label: Empirical GARCH(1,1) vs ARCH(8) example
themes.need: In the US inflation-rate application, how does a fitted GARCH(1,1) model compare to Engle-Kraft's ARCH(8) declining-lag model in diagnostics and fit?
themes.distributed_justification: The model-comparison narrative is interrupted only by the lag-comparison sentence (b040, assigned to t04) and figure-caption trash; the setup, model diagnostics, kurtosis/skewness comparison, and forecast-interval interpretation together answer one applied model-comparison question.
